chunks: A man came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and said: “O Commander of the Faithful, by Allah, I indeed love you.”
So he said to him: “But I dislike you.”
He said: “Because you seek earning through the adhan and take payment for teaching the Qur’an.”

key_terms.أَجْرًا: payment or wage taken in return
key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.أُبْغِضُكَ: I dislike you; a statement of disapproval toward the man’s conduct
key_terms.أُحِبُّكَ: I love you; an expression of claimed devotion and loyalty
key_terms.الْأَذَانِ: the call to prayer, a devotional act connected to salat
key_terms.تَعْلِيمِ الْقُرْآنِ: teaching the Qur’an, imparting sacred recitation and knowledge
key_terms.كَسْبًا: earning or profit sought as material gain

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about taking payment for the adhan and teaching the Qur’an?
ai.summary: This hadith relates that Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام reproached a man despite his claim of love because his conduct was blameworthy. The report condemns seeking material gain through the adhan and taking wages for teaching the Qur’an, highlighting the moral and legal seriousness of sincerity in acts connected to worship and sacred knowledge.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3674 - A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (as) and said:
"O Commander of the Faithful, by Allah (swt), I love you."
Imam (as) said to him: "But I dislike you."
The man asked: "Why?"
Imam (as) replied: "Because you seek profit through the call to prayer (Adhan) and take payment for teaching the Quran."
